title: Small limits, colimits and cartesian closure of the infinity category of quasicategories
statement: Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and use the quasicategory, coherent functor-category, mapping-space and colimit conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ be the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories, formed in a universe containing its objects. It admits all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits and is cartesian closed. For $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories $A,E$, the internal Hom is the coherent functor quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)$, including all coherent transformations, and there are natural equivalences $$\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(A,E))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(T\times A,E)$$ for every $T$. The colimit and exponential constructions are natural in their diagrams and remain valid after enlarging the ambient universe to contain the target quasicategory and its coherent functor categories.

source.place: Definition 3.0.0.1 and Section 3.3.3, introductory paragraph, printed p. 214: Cat_infinity has small limits and colimits computed as homotopy (co)limits in the marked cartesian model. Sections 3.1.3-3.1.4, especially Proposition 3.1.4.2 and Corollary 3.1.4.3, give cartesian compatibility and the marked internal Hom. The exponential formula is the degreewise exponential law. Corollary 4.2.4.8 gives the model presentation of small (co)limits. All constructions are relative to the chosen universes. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Work relative to $\mathcal U$, reserving a larger universe for the category of all $\mathcal U$-small objects. Let $\mathcal M$ be the category of $\mathcal U$-small marked simplicial sets with the marked model over a point of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. That statement gives a combinatorial simplicial model category, all objects cofibrant, with fibrant objects exactly $B^\natural$ for small quasicategories $B$. It also identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}})$ with $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$. In particular no model structure on unmarked simplicial sets enriched by its non-Kan functor objects is being assumed. The mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], followed by the marked model's identity for its Kan enrichment, gives natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(B,E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)^\simeq$, compatible with composition.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7; Corollary 3.1.4.4 and Remark 3.1.4.6; Proposition 1.1.5.10 and Theorem 2.2.0.1.

proof.text:
For every $\mathcal U$-small family $(A_i)_{i\in J}$, the degreewise product $\prod_i A_i$ is a quasicategory: pair the fillers of each inner horn coordinatewise. The degreewise coproduct $\coprod_i A_i$ is also a quasicategory: the edge graph of an inner horn is connected, so any horn into this coproduct lies in one summand and can be filled there. Degreewise pairing and restriction give
$$\operatorname{Fun}(T,\prod_i A_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{Fun}(T,A_i),\qquad \operatorname{Fun}(\coprod_i A_i,E)=\prod_i\operatorname{Fun}(A_i,E).$$
An edge in a product is an equivalence exactly when each coordinate is: pair the inverse edges and both triangular witnesses. Thus cores commute with these products. For the discrete shape $J$ one has $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathscr C)=\prod_{j\in J}\mathscr C$ degreewise, and a right-pinched mapping space in a degreewise product of quasicategories is the product of the coordinate mapping spaces, directly from the definition. Hence, by the mapping-space formula of step 1, the projection cone gives $\operatorname{Map}(T,\prod_iA_i)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(T,A_i)$ and the inclusion cocone gives $\operatorname{Map}(\coprod_iA_i,E)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(A_i,E)$, and the cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] and its dual make these objects, with their actual projections and inclusions, products and coproducts in $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$. This includes the empty family: $\Delta^0$ is terminal and the empty simplicial set is initial. All these simplicial sets are $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Degreewise products, coproducts, inverse-triangle witnesses; compare Scholze Lecture II basic fact (7).

proof.text: For a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $X$, use [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion] to obtain the specified $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $RX$ and inner-horn cell inclusion $j:X\to RX$. For every quasicategory $E$ in any containing universe, that node gives the right lifting property against all monomorphisms for $j^*:\operatorname{Fun}(RX,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,E)$ and says both objects are quasicategories. By the weak-factorization-system clause of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], $j^*$ is a Joyal trivial fibration. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] it has a simplicial quasi-inverse and two inverse coherent natural equivalences. All functors preserve equivalence edges by applying the functor to their inverse-triangle witnesses. Restrict the inverse maps to cores. Their natural equivalences restrict to homotopies of cores: parameter edges are equivalences because their vertex components are, using [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; each remaining edge is a composite of a parameter edge and an image of an equivalence edge, as witnessed by the defining triangles. The restricted maps and homotopies exhibit an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}(RX,E)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(X,E)^\simeq$. The same $j$ works in all larger universes by the completion node's explicit lifting assertion.

source.place: Corollaries 2.3.2.4-2.3.2.5; small-object inner-horn completion as stated in [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion]; Theorem 2.2.5.1.

proof.text:
For a span $A\leftarrow B\to C$, factor $B\to A$ by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] as $B\hookrightarrow A'\xrightarrow{q}A$, a monomorphism followed by a trivial fibration in the small universe. The composite $A'\to A\to\Delta^0$ is a fibration, so $A'$ is a quasicategory; [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] makes $q$ a functor equivalence. Form the degreewise pushout $P_0=A'\amalg_B C$ and apply step 3 to obtain $P_0\to P$. For any target quasicategory $E$ there is a restriction identity
$$\operatorname{Fun}(P_0,E)=\operatorname{Fun}(A',E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)}\operatorname{Fun}(C,E).$$
By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], the first restriction is an isofibration. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] with $Q=\Delta^0$, then step 3, to obtain
$$\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(A',E)^\simeq\mathop\times^h_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)^\simeq}\operatorname{Fun}(C,E)^\simeq.$$
These comparisons come from the pushout inclusions and their constant comparison path. Step 1 identifies this with the projection-induced mapping-space comparison of that coherent square. The square criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion], applied in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty^{\mathrm{op}}$, proves that it is a pushout of the replacement span. Finally apply that criterion's invariance under equivalences of diagrams to the map of spans $(q,1_B,1_C)$. It is an equivalence since $q$ is; the limiting cone in the opposite category therefore gives a colimiting cocone on the original span with equivalent apex. Thus the original span has a $\mathcal U$-small pushout.

source.place: Corollary 2.3.2.5; the direct pushout calculation uses Kerodon 01F1 and 033R, with the coherent cone criterion.

proof.text: For a cospan $A\to B\leftarrow C$, factor $A\to B$ in the small Joyal model as a trivial cofibration $A\to A'$ followed by a fibration $A'\to B$. Its source $A'$ is a quasicategory, and [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] identifies $A\to A'$ as a functor equivalence and $A'\to B$ as an isofibration. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit], the degreewise pullback $A'\times_B C$, with its projections, is a pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$. The theorem includes quasicategory closure and the mapping-space universal property for every test object; no fibration condition on $C\to B$ is needed. Explicitly write the original arrows as $f:A\to B$ and $g:C\to B$, the factorization as $t:A\to A'$, $p:A'\to B$ with $pt=f$, and the pullback projections as $a:D\to A'$, $c:D\to C$ with $pa=gc$. Choose a simplicial quasi-inverse $s:A'\to A$ with inverse natural equivalences $ts\simeq\operatorname{id}_{A'}$ and $st\simeq\operatorname{id}_A$. The maps $sa:D\to A$ and $c:D\to C$ form a coherent cone, with comparison $fsa=ptsa\simeq pa=gc$. For every test quasicategory $Q$, postcomposition with $t$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}(Q,A)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(Q,A')$, compatibly over $\operatorname{Map}(Q,B)$ since $pt=f$. Postcomposition with $s$ and the two chosen homotopies give its inverse on the path-space pullbacks, by applying the homotopies to the comparison paths in every simplicial degree. The displayed universal comparison for $D$ is consequently also the comparison for this original cone. The square criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion], applied to this projection-induced comparison and using its invariance under equivalences of cospan diagrams, proves that it is a pullback. All objects used are $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.28; Joyal factorization and fibration characterization as in Cisinski Theorem 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.6.

proof.text: Apply the existence clause of [lem-coef-infinity-small-colimit-generation] to $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$: step 2 supplies all $\mathcal U$-small coproducts, including the empty one, and step 4 supplies all pushouts. Thus every $\mathcal U$-small simplicial diagram has a colimit, with no ordinary-nerve restriction on its shape. Apply the same theorem to the opposite infinity category: step 2 supplies its small coproducts by products in the original category, and step 5 supplies its pushouts by pullbacks in the original category. Opposites reverse simplicial order and interchange cone and cocone conditions, so the resulting colimits are all $\mathcal U$-small limits in the original category. No new diagram-model comparison or localization theorem is used.

source.place: Theorem 7.3.22 and its opposite, printed p.356 (PDF p.371); also HTT Proposition 4.4.2.6.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)$ is a quasicategory. It is $\mathcal U$-small when $A,E$ are, because in each degree its simplices are a subset of the set of maps between two $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets. Construct the exponential comparison before passing to cores: for each $n$, curry a map $T\times\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)$ to a map $A\times T\times\Delta^n\to E$ by evaluation, and permute the first two factors. To spell out the inverse, given $v:A\times T\times\Delta^n\to E$, its image at an $m$-simplex $(t,u)$ of $T\times\Delta^n$ is the map $A\times\Delta^m\to E$ whose value at an $r$-simplex $(a,\theta:[r]\to[m])$ is $v_r(a,T(\theta)t,u\theta)$. Evaluation in the other direction sends $(a,t,u)$ in degree $m$ to the value of the map $h_m(t,u)$ at $(a,\operatorname{id}_{[m]})$. These formulas are inverse by simplicial naturality and commute with restriction along every $[m]\to[n]$. They give a natural simplicial isomorphism $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(A,E))\cong\operatorname{Fun}(T\times A,E)$. In particular every edge and every higher coherent transformation is retained.

source.place: Internal-Hom construction in Section 3.1.3; direct degreewise exponential calculation from the functor simplicial-set definition. Functor closure: Scholze Lecture II, basic fact (1), printed p.14.

proof.text: The simplicial isomorphism of step 7 preserves equivalence edges and their inverse-triangle witnesses in both directions, so restricts to an isomorphism on cores. Combine this with step 1 to obtain natural mapping-space equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(A,E))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(T\times A,E)$. The map is induced by the actual evaluation functor $\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)\times A\to E$. Naturality is on mapping Kan complexes, not just components: precomposition in $T,A$ and postcomposition in $E$ commute with the evaluation and currying formulas for every simplex. The product functor is itself coherent: on mapping Kan complexes send a simplex $h$ to $h\times\operatorname{id}_A$; this respects identities and composition degreewise, hence induces a functor on coherent nerves. For each $E$ this represents the presheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(T\times A,E)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] in a larger pair of universes containing $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$ as a small simplicial set, so that its small-mapping-space hypothesis holds. By that criterion, these representing objects assemble to a coherent right adjoint of $(-)\times A$; its counit is the displayed evaluation map. With the product verified in step 2, this is precisely the cartesian internal-Hom universal property. The stronger, un-cored isomorphism in step 7 proves the displayed functor-quasicategory equivalence in the statement.

source.place: Section 3.1.3 internal Homs; Proposition 3.1.4.2 and Corollary 3.1.4.3; elementary restriction of the explicit exponential isomorphism to cores.

proof.text:
For a fixed $\mathcal U$-small simplicial shape $K$, step 6 supplies colimiting cocones and limiting cones for every diagram $p:K\to\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], their universal maps give the natural mapping-space representations
$$\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{colim}p,E)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)}(p,\Delta_K E),\qquad\operatorname{Map}(E,\operatorname{lim}p)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)}(\Delta_K E,p).$$
Apply respectively the left- and right-adjoint clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] to the constant-diagram functor. Choose a larger pair of universes in which both its source and target fit as small simplicial sets; their mapping spaces are then small. The criterion assembles these representing objects and universal maps into coherent colimit and limit functors and their units and counits, including all transformations. The contractibility assertion of the cone-calculus statement gives independence of the universal choices. The exponential comparison in step 7 is already natural in every simplicial parameter, and step 8 assembles its right adjoint coherently. Thus naturality does not depend on assuming that ordinary model replacements are enriched functors.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4.3 and its dual; Proposition 5.2.4.2 and its opposite.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal V$ contain $\mathcal U$ and any additional target quasicategory under consideration. The inclusion $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}\to\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal V}$ is induced on coherent nerves by the enriched inclusion: its mapping Kan complexes on the old objects are identical, since simplicial map sets, equivalence witnesses and composition are unchanged. Step 2's coproduct and product formulas are valid against any $\mathcal V$-small test object. The pushout construction of step 4 is also still universal there: the monomorphism $B\hookrightarrow A'$ is unchanged; the equivalence $A'\to A$ retains its simplicial quasi-inverse and inverse-triangle witnesses; the same degreewise pushout $P_0$ and same small inner-horn cell replacement $P_0\to P$ have the mapping property of step 3 against all $\mathcal V$-small targets. The exponentiation and isofibration-pullback statements used in the calculation apply in $\mathcal V$. Thus the inclusion preserves the constructed small coproducts and pushouts. The preservation clause of [lem-coef-infinity-small-colimit-generation] now proves that it preserves every $\mathcal U$-small colimit, including its cocone. For completeness it also preserves products and pullbacks: the isofibration of step 5 is characterized by finite horns and equivalence lifts, so remains an isofibration, and its degreewise pullback and comparison remain the same. The opposite preservation criterion gives the limit assertion as well. Finally step 7's sets of simplicial maps, evaluation, restrictions and currying formulas are identical under enlargement, so the internal Hom and its full coherent exponential comparison remain valid. This proves precisely the claimed universe clause without calling a large diagram small.
